Task: Build React account status OFFLINE health and stock watchlist views
Description: Build the top-level React App shell, the global status header/banner, the account KPI ribbon, the health summary and the stock watchlist.

Before editing, inspect: mike_trade/dashboard/api.py (r.1) for the exact endpoint paths and response fields; dashboard/frontend/src/main.tsx, vite.config.ts and tsconfig.json (r.2); and the CLI/Makefile command names to display as operator guidance.

Shared contract with r.4 (r.4 runs concurrently, so do not create r.4's files):
- dashboard/frontend/src/api/client.ts exports typed functions listAccounts(), getStatus(accountId), getKpis(accountId), getWatchlist(accountId), getHealth(accountId), getSymbolDetail(accountId, symbol), getAccountDetail(accountId), plus the matching response TypeScript types and an ApiError class.
- dashboard/frontend/src/components/SymbolDetails.tsx exports a default component with props { accountId: string; symbol: string; onClose: () => void }.
- dashboard/frontend/src/components/AccountDetail.tsx exports AccountSelector with props { selectedAccountId: string | null; onSelect: (accountId: string) => void } and a default AccountDetail component with props { accountId: string }.
Import only these names.

Implement dashboard/frontend/src/App.tsx:
(1) Holds selectedAccountId and selectedSymbol state. Switching accounts discards all previously fetched account-scoped state before rendering new data, so values from different accounts/modes/scenarios are never rendered together.
(2) Polls status/kpis/watchlist/health on a bounded interval with AbortController cancellation on account switch.
(3) The global header shows the selected account/scenario and a prominent mode badge (LIVE/PAPER/SHADOW, with LIVE visually distinct); engine state RUNNING/PAUSED/DEGRADED/OFFLINE/RECONCILING; a live heartbeat age; broker and data connectivity/freshness; market OPEN/CLOSED/HALTED; exchange clock (America/New_York); next entry cutoff; entries-allowed reasons.
(4) Heartbeat age keeps ticking client-side between polls from last_heartbeat_at relative to server_time offset. The UI shows OFFLINE once that age exceeds the threshold even if the next poll has not arrived. If the dashboard API itself is unreachable, it shows a distinct DASHBOARD API UNREACHABLE banner.
(5) A STALE watermark overlays last-known values whenever engine_state is OFFLINE or a value has fresh=false.
(6) The KPI ribbon shows cash, buying power, equity, total budget, reserved pending buys, deployed capital, open positions, pending orders, daily realized/unrealized P&L, lifetime P&L, unresolved protection/data/reconciliation error counts and provenance/as-of. Decimal strings are displayed as-is, without float arithmetic.
(7) A health panel shows feed age/reconnects/subscriptions, broker status/rate errors, scheduler lag, persistence/backup state, last reconciliation and actionable errors with the CLI/Make command text.

Implement dashboard/frontend/src/components/Watchlist.tsx:
- A table of up to 10 symbol rows with every watchlist field from the API: price/bid/ask, data age and stale flag; composite phase; active BUY/SELL strategies; next due trigger/last evaluation; last signal with accepted/rejected reason; confirmed qty/cost basis/purchase time; budget/commitment/planned loss; daily entry count/cap; loss streak/lockout/reset mode; cooldown/next eligible; minimum-hold remaining; entry cutoff; protection mode/status/price/quantity; native broker HWM labeled 'broker HWM' vs stepped local anchor labeled 'stepped anchor'; desired vs confirmed stop; last protection update; realized/unrealized/lifetime P&L.
- Shows a coverage warning when protection quantity differs from confirmed quantity.
- Clicking a row calls onSelectSymbol.

Implement dashboard/frontend/src/styles.css: restrained operational styling with clear state colors for OFFLINE/DEGRADED/STALE/LIVE, readable tables and a responsive layout. No charts.

No element may submit orders or change configuration. Where an action is relevant, render the CLI/Make command text in a <code> element.
Phase: R
Acceptance criteria:
  - App.tsx renders a header with mode badge, engine state, ticking heartbeat age, broker/data freshness, market state, exchange clock, next entry cutoff and a STALE watermark when engine_state is OFFLINE or values have fresh=false
  - The client-side heartbeat age turns the header OFFLINE once the age exceeds the API-provided threshold without waiting for a new engine flag; an unreachable dashboard API shows a distinct unreachable banner
  - Account switching clears previously loaded account-scoped KPI, watchlist and health state and aborts in-flight requests before showing the newly selected account
  - The KPI ribbon displays all listed account KPIs with provenance/as-of, rendering Decimal strings without parseFloat/Number arithmetic on money values
  - Watchlist.tsx renders up to 10 rows with every listed per-symbol field, separately labels broker HWM vs stepped anchor and desired vs confirmed stop, and flags protection quantity that differs from confirmed quantity
  - Budget, entry cutoff, lockout, cooldown and minimum-hold reasons are visible per symbol row
  - No button, form or fetch call in these files uses a non-GET method; operator actions are shown only as CLI/Make command text
  - Only App.tsx, Watchlist.tsx and styles.css are written; imports from r.4 files match the shared contract names exactly

# AGENTS.md

## Purpose

This repository is operated by an autonomous multi-agent system (abracapocus_2).
All agents must follow these rules when modifying the codebase.

---

## Core Principles

- Minimal blast radius: only modify what is required for the task
- Deterministic verification: all changes must be verifiable via code (tests, compile, scripts)
- No architecture drift: do not introduce new frameworks or major design changes unless explicitly required
- No unrelated refactors
- All changes must be reproducible from a clean clone

---

## Project Structure

- docs/ → design, plans, architecture constraints
- plans/ → master plans
- phases/ → phase definitions
- tasks/ → executable task documents
- backends/ → CLI backend adapters
- agents/ → specialist agents
- runtime/ → orchestration, routing, state
- reports/ → execution reports (DO NOT MODIFY MANUALLY)
- state/runtime_state.json → runtime state (DO NOT COMMIT)

---

## Task Execution Rules

- Always operate from a task document when available
- Respect:
  - selected_backend
  - verification_profile
  - acceptance_criteria
- If a task conflicts with architecture constraints or phase scope:
  - STOP and report conflict

---

## Backend Rules

- Backends must:
  - execute commands deterministically
  - capture stdout, stderr, exit_code
  - not silently fail
- Do not invent backend interfaces; use existing adapters
- Codex CLI, Aider, Gemini, Claude Code should be invoked through backends only

---

## Verification Rules

- Verification must be deterministic
- Preferred checks:
  - pytest
  - python -m py_compile
- Do not rely on model self-evaluation

---

## Execution Control Flow (PERMANENT ARCHITECTURAL RULE)

**HEURISTIC INFERENCE MUST NEVER PARTICIPATE IN ABRACAPOCUS EXECUTION CONTROL FLOW.**

Abracapocus must not determine execution success, failure, acceptance,
rejection, blocking, retry eligibility, phase progression, or completion from
heuristic inference. A heuristic is any conclusion that is *inferred* rather
than *directly established by an explicit executable contract or a concrete
runtime fact*.

Runtime status is derived ONLY from concrete, mechanically observable facts:

1. The backend process exit code. A backend that exits `0` (with no hard
   write-policy violation) is a successful execution.
2. Objectively observed hard write-policy violations (changed paths outside the
   declared allowed write paths).
3. Explicit operator-authored commands (task/phase verification the plan
   explicitly contains). Their raw results are reported, kept DISTINCT from
   backend execution status.
4. Objective orchestrator failures with direct evidence (backend could not
   launch, required document could not be parsed, subprocess infrastructure
   failed).

**Verification results are observational and must not rewrite backend execution
status.** A verifier returning non-zero must NEVER, by itself, turn a
successful backend execution into unverified, stop a phase, or trigger an
automatic rerun. Verification is the result of a command, not authority to
rewrite history.

**Execution control:** Task-local problems (non-zero exit, timeout,
write-policy violation, frame failure, backend launch failure) produce
acceptance status ``"unverified"`` with truthful evidence preserved. They
MUST NOT stop sibling tasks, later phases, or the plan. Only operator
cancellation (SIGINT/SIGTERM/dashboard cancel) may terminate a run
(acceptance status ``"interrupted"``). Dependencies are ordering constraints,
not acceptance gates — any terminal attempt outcome satisfies a dependency
edge. The status ``"failed"`` is banned from acceptance output.

Do NOT reintroduce -- under any name, feature flag, "advisory" wrapper, or
compatibility mode -- context completeness/sufficiency scoring, change or
architecture assessment used as a gate, intent/scope matching, reconciliation
gates, no-progress judgments, confidence/risk scores, model/LLM/reviewer
judgments over status, shadow/adaptive/secondary-verification gates, or
heuristic retry/failure-classification control flow. Failure classification may
only *summarize* an already-established concrete failure; it must never create
one. Retries are permitted only for explicitly defined mechanical backend
failures. Future agents must not add these systems back.

---

## Git Rules

- Do not commit:
  - runtime_state.json
  - reports/
  - logs/
  - virtual environments
- Do not modify .gitignore unless required by task
- Do not create excessive commits; prefer grouped logical commits

---

## Allowed Changes

- Implement task requirements
- Fix failing verification
- Update relevant tests
- Improve documentation tied to the task

---

## Forbidden Changes

- Changing architecture without explicit instruction
- Adding dependencies without justification
- Modifying unrelated files
- Deleting important files
- Bypassing verification

---

## Planning Rules

- Plans are multi-phase
- Completed sections are immutable
- Remaining sections may be updated
- Tasks must align with:
  - project brief
  - architecture constraints
  - active phase

---

## Reporting

- All executions must produce structured reports
- Reports must include:
  - changed files
  - verification results
  - assessment

---

## Behavior

- Do not ask unnecessary questions
- Do not stall execution
- Do not perform broad scans unless required
- Prefer direct action over analysis

---

## Priority Order

This ordering guides *implementation decisions* only. It does NOT make
verification an acceptance authority: verification results are observational
(see "Execution Control Flow"), and never override a concrete backend
execution result.

1. Architecture constraints
2. Task definition
3. Verification results (observational signal, not acceptance authority)
4. Plan guidance

If conflicts occur, follow this order.
